facility: Kansas State University campus chilled water system, Manhattan, Kansas
source: Stanley Consultants, Kansas State University Chilled Water Master Plan, March 2013 (public university document)
question: The campus chilled water load is projected to grow to about 11,384 tons by 2025. Does the existing chilled water production and distribution (chillers, pumps, loops, cross-connections) maintain N+1 capacity through 2025? What limits it, when, and what should be built or upgraded (chillers, plants, piping), with order-of-magnitude costs?

criteria.value: Maintain N+1 reliability for chilled water production; N+1 attained when design capacity is met with largest chiller out of service

criteria.name: Design specific flow

rfi.issue: No metered peak or historical plant data to verify JCI 2010 + SF/ton load estimates
rfi.reason: Report states no historical data or metering exists; peak inferred from staff interviews of 2011 operation (p.15,p.17)
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Accept reported 5480 tons peak (7307 x 0.75) and 5400-ton operating check as baseline, with metering to be used later to verify; reason is document directs future verification with new metering data

rfi.issue: Withheld recommendation clauses likely contain costs/schedule; no capital costs in available pages
rfi.reason: Cost to build/upgrade chillers, plants, piping not stated in pages 11-27,41-49
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Note costs as missing and to be developed in later steps from industry benchmarks; do not invent costs in register; reason is no source data available

rfi.issue: 2017 and 2025 summed tables vs reported totals differ (~100-300 tons)
rfi.reason: Table sums exceed reported 11928 and 15178, likely due to Kramer/Marlatt/Goodnow removals and rounding
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Use reported totals 11928 tons (2017) and 15178 tons (2025) and peaks 8946 and 11384 tons as governing; reason is report explicitly states those totals with diversity

rfi.issue: Primary/secondary pump head adequacy for expanded distant loops unknown
rfi.reason: Report warns frictional losses may grow to exceed design head (p.25) but gives only flow/head per pump (40-90 ft), no system curves
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Treat 90 ft secondary and 40/70 ft primary heads as nameplate only; flag head/friction analysis as further study; reason is insufficient hydraulic data

rfi.issue: Ages/refurbishment history for CT5-10 and condenser water pumps unknown
rfi.reason: Only states age similar to Chillers #5-7 and 20-year median life for pumps
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Assume CT5-10 internals need replacement before 2025 and condenser pumps need review at 20 years; reason follows report guidance

rfi.issue: Throckmorton CHW line noted undersized; other bottleneck sizes not quantified
rfi.reason: Appendix A notes Throckmorton line undersized; drawings show upsizes (e.g., Increase CHW to 18in) but no calculations
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: List upsizes and 18-in cross-connects as proposed mitigations to be hydraulically verified later; reason is drawings are planning-level

responses.issue: Future secondary additions 2x4000 gpm by 2017 and 4x4000 gpm by 2025 are ASSUMPTIONs without source; firm totals 22432 gpm and 26334 gpm are therefore planning proxies, not document-verified requirements.

responses.explanation: Agreed: no capital costs in pp.11-27,41-49; p.24 notes high electrical cost but no dollars. All cost_basis retained as ASSUMPTION order-of-magnitude ranges only for planning comparison. Recommendation to build is based on N+1 shortfall (6050 tons p.13 vs 8946 tons p.22 and 11384 tons p.24), not on cost justification; detailed cost estimate required.
responses.issue: Order-of-magnitude costs (>$10M chillers/plants, $1M-$10M pumping/piping) are invented benchmarks with no source data; study conclusion on what should be built cannot be cost-justified from available pages.

responses.explanation: Agreed and scope limited: BASE-SEC-FULL2 14551.6 gpm (run output) vs 14600 gpm (p.14) -0.33%, BASE-SEC-FIRM 11654.3 gpm vs 11680 gpm (p.14) -0.22%, BASE-PRI-FIRM 11740.8 gpm vs 11800 gpm (p.14) -0.51% verify header nameplate summation only. They do not prove satellite near Wind Erosion Lab (p.24) or extended-loop head adequacy. p.25 warns frictional losses may exceed design head (90-ft secondary p.14, 40/70-ft primary p.14). responses.issue: Hydraulic models verify nameplate summation only (e.g., 11654.3 vs 11680 gpm -0.22%, 11740.8 vs 11800 gpm -0.5%), not loop friction/head for satellite plant near Wind Erosion Lab (p.24) and extended distances; future firm adequacy through 2025 not hydraulically proven.

responses.explanation: Retained 2 gpm/ton (p.18) for peak sizing; 17892 gpm 2017 (ASSUMPTION: 8946 tons p.22 x2) and 22768 gpm 2025 (ASSUMPTION: 11384 tons p.24 x2). Low-delta 3.5 gpm/ton (p.18) would be ~31311 gpm in 2017 and ~39844 gpm in 2025 (ASSUMPTION arithmetic), exceeding proxies 18503.7 gpm and 26473.8 gpm. responses.issue: Peak flow proxy assumes 2 gpm/ton maintained; low delta-T risk at peak not evaluated. If delta-T degrades, even expanded pumping is undersized. Report says low delta-T most likely at low load (p.18), but no peak delta-T verification with metering (p.15).
